definition: Arbitrarily means in a way based on random choice or personal whim rather than any reason, rule, or system.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word arbitrarily. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know arbitrarily should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The substitute teacher assigned seats arbitrarily, pulling names from a coffee mug without a glance at the seating chart.
Doing something casually just means doing it in a relaxed, informal way, while doing it arbitrarily means there is no reason or rule behind the choice at all.
A rule applied arbitrarily follows whim instead of reason, but a rule applied lawlessly ignores even the authority of law itself.

Randomly means determined by pure chance — a coin flip, names from a hat, a lottery. Arbitrarily is broader and more critical: the choice follows someone's whim or convenience rather than any reason or rule. A random draw at least treats everyone alike; an arbitrary ruling just follows the chooser's mood.

Whimsically means on a playful, fanciful impulse, and it sounds light and harmless. Arbitrarily is the harsher word: it criticizes a decision that deserved a reason and got none. A cafe menu named whimsically is charming; a fine imposed arbitrarily is unjust.

The two firms settled their contract fight through arbitration, handing the decision to a private judge, the very arbiter named by the Latin root.
Arbitrarily means in a way based on random choice or personal whim rather than any reason, rule, or system.
A new manager at a shipping warehouse decided which employees got weekend shifts by dealing out playing cards: red card, you worked; black card, you stayed home.
Seniority, family obligations, and even who had volunteered made no difference at all.
Workers did not object to weekend shifts themselves, but they resented that the schedule was set arbitrarily, with no reason or rule anyone could point to.
A rotation list posted the next month fixed the problem overnight.
The shifts were assigned by random card colors rather than by any rule or reason, which is exactly what it means to decide something arbitrarily.
neutral, academic and everyday register
Arbitrarily is an adverb, so it describes how an action is done: rules enforced arbitrarily, numbers chosen arbitrarily, prices set arbitrarily.
It usually carries a critical edge, hinting that a decision deserved a reason and got none.

When the amusement park hired extra staff for the summer, every teenager wanted the same two weekends off.
The scheduling fell to Mr.
Voss, who kept no sign-up sheet, held no drawing, and published no rule.
